question: What defines a re-emerging infectious disease in a population?

options.A: An illness that was declining but is now increasing again
options.B: A completely novel pathogen discovered through genomic sequencing
options.C: A chronic non-communicable disease with sudden acute flare-ups
options.D: An inherited genetic disorder presenting with infectious symptoms

explanation: Re-emerging diseases are known infections that previously showed a decrease in cases but are now rising again. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is the distinction between emerging and re-emerging infections important for nurses?

options.A: It helps target surveillance and early recognition of unusual disease clusters
options.B: It eliminates the need for standard personal protective equipment
options.C: It determines whether the patient requires mandatory surgical intervention
options.D: It dictates the exact antibiotic dosage required for patient survival

explanation: Recognizing disease patterns aids nurses in identifying outbreaks early at the primary care level. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h1)

question: The rapid spread of infectious diseases across continents is primarily driven by what factor?
explanation: Global mobility enables infected persons and vectors to cross borders rapidly. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h2)

question: Deforestation contributes to the emergence of new infections by doing what?

options.A: Purifying local water sources to eliminate bacterial pathogens
options.B: Destroying all known viruses permanently within the soil
options.C: Forcing animal reservoirs into closer contact with human populations
options.D: Enhancing the immune systems of local rural communities

explanation: Habitat disruption brings wildlife vectors closer to human settlements, facilitating zoonotic spillover. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h2)

question: Lassa fever is primarily transmitted to humans through contact with what animal vector?
explanation: The rodent Mastomys natalensis serves as the primary reservoir and vector for the Lassa virus. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h3)

question: A community experiences a sudden cholera outbreak during heavy seasonal rains. What is the most likely primary cause?

options.A: Direct contact with infected rodent droppings
options.D: A sudden mutation in the local mosquito population

explanation: Cholera is a waterborne disease that spreads rapidly when heavy rains contaminate drinking water sources. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h3)

question: Airborne transmission differs from droplet transmission because airborne pathogens are spread via what mechanism?

options.A: Ingestion of contaminated food or municipal water
options.B: Direct physical contact with an infected person's skin
options.C: Small aerosolized nuclei that remain suspended in the air
options.D: Large respiratory particles that drop quickly to the floor

explanation: Airborne droplets are tiny and stay suspended longer, traveling greater distances than large respiratory droplets. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary role of a vector in infectious disease transmission?

options.A: Bridging the transmission gap between infected and susceptible hosts
options.B: Filtering pathogens out of contaminated municipal water supplies
options.C: Producing chemical toxins that weaken the human immune system
options.D: Acting as the primary site for bacterial spore germination

explanation: Vectors like mosquitoes carry pathogens from one host to another, facilitating spread. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which symptom is commonly observed during the early stage of many emerging viral infections?

options.C: Localized joint stiffness in the hands

explanation: Fever and muscle pain are classic early systemic signs of many viral pathogens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h5)

question: A patient presents with fever and fatigue. What essential piece of history must the nurse collect first?

options.B: Detailed dietary preferences over the last decade
options.C: Recent travel history and potential local exposures
options.D: Family history of chronic cardiovascular disease

explanation: Travel and exposure history provide critical clues for identifying potential emerging infectious threats. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which laboratory test is commonly used to detect viral RNA in suspected emerging infections?
explanation: PCR assays amplify genetic material to accurately confirm the presence of viral pathogens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is proper specimen collection and handling vital when dealing with dangerous pathogens?

options.A: To speed up routine administrative discharge paperwork for patients
options.B: To eliminate the need for any subsequent confirmatory blood tests
options.C: To prevent accidental exposure of staff and ensure valid test results
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of operating the hospital laboratory

explanation: Strict biosafety during collection protects healthcare workers and preserves specimen integrity. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which practice is classified as a standard precaution for all hospitalized patients?

options.A: Restricting all family visitors from the hospital ward
options.B: Wearing sterile surgical gowns for routine vital signs
options.C: Placing every patient in a negative pressure room
options.D: Performing proper hand hygiene before and after care

explanation: Hand hygiene is the fundamental standard precaution required for every patient encounter. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: Cohorting patients on an infectious disease ward involves which of the following strategies?

options.A: Mixing uninfected patients with high-risk cases to build immunity
options.B: Isolating each patient in a separate building outside the hospital
options.C: Placing patients with the same confirmed infection in the same area
options.D: Transferring all recovering patients home regardless of status

explanation: Cohorting groups patients with identical infections together to optimize barrier nursing care. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: When is antiviral therapy like ribavirin most effective for treating Lassa fever?

options.A: During the late convalescent phase after fever has resolved
options.B: Exclusively as a prophylactic dose before any exposure occurs
options.C: When administered early in the course of the disease
options.D: Only after the patient develops complete multi-organ failure

explanation: Early administration of antivirals significantly reduces viral replication and improves survival rates. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h8)

question: Why is meticulous fluid balance monitoring essential during supportive care for severe infections?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory can calculate daily blood cell counts
options.B: To determine the exact discharge date for administrative records
options.C: To prevent complications such as fluid overload or dehydration
options.D: To eliminate the need for checking vital signs every shift

explanation: Careful monitoring ensures patients receive adequate hydration without tipping into pulmonary edema. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of public health disease surveillance?

options.A: Providing financial loans for private hospital infrastructural upgrades
options.B: Managing routine human resource schedules for nursing staff
options.C: Continuous collection and analysis of data to guide disease control
options.D: Punishing healthcare facilities that fail to meet hygiene quotas

explanation: Surveillance tracks disease trends to inform timely public health interventions and policy decisions. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h9)

question: A nurse suspects a case of a rare notifiable haemorrhagic fever in the ward. What action should be taken next?

options.A: Report the case immediately through proper public health channels
options.B: Discharge the patient quietly to avoid panic in the hospital
options.C: Wait until laboratory confirmation is 100 percent certain before acting
options.D: Post details of the case on personal social media platforms

explanation: Suspected cases of notifiable diseases must be reported instantly to trigger rapid public health containment. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h9)
